column1: # Reviewed specimen previews: three per model, shown on hover in the project-type
# and model pickers. Columns: id, model, projectType, imageId, width, height,
# HOW THESE WERE CHOSEN. `select.sql` ranks production segmentations by the
# model's OWN mean confidence (>= 0.9) inside a per-model object-count band, and
# every survivor was rendered at the real 150 px tile size and looked at (see
# README). Ranking by polygon count — the obvious first idea — selects the
# WORST rows for the spheroid models: a high count means the model was tracing
# debris, and the contact sheet was red scribble. Confidence is in the stored
# `origin=infer` rows are the three models with no usable production output
# (neurite_soma has none at all, mamba_unet had 1 row, cbam_resunet 2). Their
# polygons come from running THAT model on a real frame through the ML service
# (`infer-missing.sh`) — never from a sibling model, so every tile shows the
# output of the model it is filed under. mamba_unet's one production row is
# additionally UNUSABLE as a picture — a lone 205-px spheroid in a 2048-px
# frame, which the sizing rule can only render at 20 px of a 150-px tile — so
# all three of its tiles are inferred on real frames instead.
